The single failure is a CRITICAL route-ordering bug where /api/articles/most-read is shadowed by /api/articles/{slug} declared 130 lines earlier — most-read endpoint returns 404 'Artículo no encontrado'. This cascades into the frontend: the new 'Lo más leído' section on the Home page silently fails to render (network panel shows 2x 404 on /api/articles/most-read?limit=4). Make.com automation gate: no-key=401, wrong-key=401, correct-key=200 (Claude generation succeeded — LLM budget is healthy now, not exhausted). Hero singleton enforcement: setting hero=true on article B correctly flipped hero=false on article A (verified via /api/articles/featured). Email fire-and-forget: newsletter subscribe response time 311ms, login response 268ms — both well under 1500ms threshold so Resend is non-blocking. Frontend verified: Home stats strip shows '67.801 LECTURAS / 5254 SUSCRIPTORES / 8 HISTORIAS' in serif font on dark band; Footer is dark (#0d0d0f) with white text, NOXEAL logo, hola@noxeal.com mailto, 4 social icons with correct hrefs (instagram.com/noxael18, x.com/noxeal, tiktok.com/@noxael18, youtube.com/@noxeal); Article detail shows '1501 lecturas' counter and view-tracking POST fires (article views went 1501→1502 on visit); Newsletter form shows '¡Suscripción confirmada!' green sonner toast on submit; Admin panel has all 6 tabs (Artículos, Generar con IA, Comentarios, Suscriptores, Usuarios, Make.com), Make.com tab renders endpoint URLs + X-API-Key reference + 4 copy buttons + body JSON example + flow recommendations + security warning; admin article rows show 'Marcar hero' and 'Marcar trending' toggle buttons (10 of each on the list view), with active state pills 'Hero' on libro-negro-digital-epstein and 'Trending' on the appropriate articles. IA + Editor badge correctly absent on non-AI articles and present in admin DRAFT pills (IA tag visible on Make.com refuerza... and TikTok y la Generación Z drafts).

critical.issue: Route is shadowed by /api/articles/{slug} which is declared earlier in server.py (line 264 vs line 394). FastAPI matches routes in declaration order, so the literal path 'most-read' is captured as a {slug} parameter and the slug-finder returns 404 'Artículo no encontrado'. Frontend Home 'Lo más leído' section silently fails (2x 404 in network panel). FIX: move @api_router.get('/articles/most-read') ABOVE @api_router.get('/articles/{slug}') in server.py, or rename the route to /api/articles-most-read or /api/articles/_most-read. Same hazard applies to /articles/featured (line 253) which luckily was declared BEFORE /articles/{slug} so it works — keep that pattern.

minor.issue: After hero singleton test, the test restores hero=true on libro-negro-digital-epstein (default). If a future test reorders, default hero may shift — fine for now.

ui_bugs.issue: Section silently does not render because GET /api/articles/most-read?limit=4 returns 404 (see CRITICAL backend bug). After the backend route ordering is fixed, this section should appear automatically — frontend code path is correct but receives empty array on 404.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend handles the 404 gracefully (no crash, no console error spam beyond the network failure log) but also no fallback — section is just absent. Consider rendering a skeleton or hiding numerically only when data.length>0 (which is the current behavior, just confusingly invisible).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py route ordering: /articles/{slug} at line 264 captures literal sub-paths declared after it (most-read at 394). FastAPI does NOT auto-prioritize literal paths — fix declaration order or use distinct prefixes.
/api/automation/articles/generate has NO rate limit. A leaked MAKE_API_KEY would allow unlimited Claude calls draining EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget. Add a per-key throttle (eg. 10 articles/hour).
email_service notify_admin_* functions are fired via background tasks but should also have a bounded thread pool to prevent unbounded task accumulation if Resend is slow/down.
/api/public-stats hardcodes boost values 47230 / 5247 in code. Consider moving to env so they can be incremented over time without redeploy.

/api/feed.rss generates XML via string concatenation — works but vulnerable to XML-injection if any article title/category contains special chars (<, >, &). Use xml.etree.ElementTree or feedgen library.
server.py is now ~1048 lines — split into routers/{auth,articles,admin,automation,seo,public}.py. Mixing public + admin + automation in one file makes auth surface harder to audit.
MAKE_API_KEY is checked via constant string compare — could leak via timing. Use hmac.compare_digest.

PUBLIC_STATUS_FILTER must include status:'published' check on increment_view path — currently it does (verified) but make sure unpublishing an article also stops view increments (it does — confirmed by 200 + ok:false on filter mismatch).

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: /app/backend/server.py declares @api_router.get('/articles/{slug}') at line 264 and @api_router.get('/articles/most-read') at line 394. FastAPI/Starlette matches routes in registration order — so a request to /api/articles/most-read is matched against the {slug} pattern first, slug='most-read' is passed to get_article_by_slug(slug), which queries db.articles for {'slug':'most-read'} → returns nothing → raises HTTPException(404, 'Artículo no encontrado'). REPRODUCTION: curl https://trending-news-3.preview.emergentagent.com/api/articles/most-read?limit=4 → 404 {detail:'Artículo no encontrado'}. MITIGATION: move the most-read decorator + function definition above the slug decorator (literal paths must precede parameterized paths), OR rename the route to /api/articles-most-read or /api/most-read. Same fix already worked for /articles/featured and /articles/{slug}/related which are declared BEFORE the {slug} catch-all (related uses /{slug}/related so the suffix differentiates it; featured uses literal 'featured' before {slug} — that pattern works). After fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4.py::test_most_read_top_n; expected to pass and Home 'Lo más leído' section will render automatically without any frontend change.
